A commissioned reply follows, כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֹ֣ל בַּרְזֶ֡ל נָתַ֜תִּי עַל צַוַּ֣אר כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה לַעֲבֹ֛ד אֶת נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל (oshb:Jer.28.14, byte), matching “For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says,” “I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon” (web:Jer.28.14) — the same defective, vav-less spelling of Nebuchadnezzar’s name recurs in this reply as it did in the claim it answers. Verse 15 turns from Yahweh’s commissioned word to Jeremiah’s own delivery of it, marked by the same reply-formula that opened his first answer to Hananiah at verse 5, so the row is held to this commissioned content alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this unit through Jeremiah’s own confrontation of Hananiah in verses 15 and 16 was rejected because the narration there reopens with the said-to-Hananiah formula that marked his first reply at verse 5 — the two openings re-collate at accent_stripped tier — a scene-level shift from Yahweh’s private commission to Jeremiah to Jeremiah’s own public delivery of it.
